original.target_description: Study 1, point-biserial correlation between conception risk and intention to vote for Barack Obama (1=Obama, 0=all other options), in the university sample of white women. Located on PDF-text page 3, printed page 396, section 2.2.

n.sample_role: Analytic participants: white women aged 18–22 in Study 1; section 2.1.1 explicitly identifies observations included in the analyses below.
n.exclusions: Data culled to white US citizens without chronic health problems, with normal-length menstrual cycles, not pregnant, willing to state voting preference, and not using hormonal contraceptives. Exclusion counts are not printed.
n.location: Printed p. 396 (third article page), section 2.1.1 Research subjects; section 2.2 Results
n.quote: described below include observations from 62 white women

es.location: Printed p. 396 (third article page), section 2.2 Results

p.location: Unassigned field; placeholder only. Same-test printed p=.03 retained in es.test_statistic and notes.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: matching title Fertility and race perception predict voter preference for Barack Obama; authors Carlos David Navarrete, Melissa M. McDonald, Michael L. Mott, Joseph Cesario, Robert Sapolsky; Evolution and Human Behavior 31 (2010) 394–399; DOI 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2010.05.002. Text is the full primary Original Article, including Methods, Results, and references. No PDF path supplied, so no PDF rendering was possible or performed. Locator p. 3 maps to printed p. 396, where section 2.2 reports the Study 1 correlation; Study 2 results occur on the next page. Target selected by page, study section, and test description, without numeric matching or row order. N=62 is explicitly the sample included in the analyses, not inferred from r notation or degrees of freedom; no arithmetic derivation. Same-test p is printed as p=.03 (exact equality); p_o is unassigned and remains a placeholder. Only n_o and es_value_o assigned; other fields are placeholders.
